workflows.name: aws-one-way-door
workflows.description: Amazon Working Backwards with one-way-door ceremony — for hard-to-reverse decisions (typically new product lines, public commitments, major investments). Starts with the human-authored Press Release (the founding artifact), stress-tests it with the FAQ, and requires the 6-pager decision narrative before build spend. Optional post-FAQ deepening: MRD (market validation, product scale) or OpportunitySpec (discovery, feature scale) — the door sets the ceremony; the scale picks the tool.

principles.name: Customer Obsession
principles.description: Start with the customer and work backwards; earn and keep customer trust. Economics count: exciting customers with something unsustainable is not doing right by them. Competitors inform, customers decide.

principles.name: Ownership
principles.description: Think long-term; never sacrifice long-term value for short-term results. Act for the whole company. The test: what would I do if this were my personal money?

principles.name: Invent And Simplify
principles.description: Expect invention and simplification; be externally aware and take ideas from everywhere — no 'not invented here.' Accept being misunderstood for long periods.

principles.name: Are Right A Lot
principles.description: Judgment over ego: seek diverse perspectives and work to disconfirm your own beliefs. The goal is the best answer for the customer, whoever's idea it is. Leaders speak last.

principles.name: Learn And Be Curious
principles.description: Never done learning; curious about new possibilities and act to explore them.

principles.name: Hire And Develop The Best
principles.description: Raise the performance bar with every hire; develop leaders and take ownership of others' growth.

principles.name: Insist On Highest Standards
principles.description: Relentlessly, even unreasonably, high standards. Defects do not get sent down the line. Higher expectations produce better results.

principles.name: Think Big
principles.description: Thinking small is a self-fulfilling prophecy. Communicate a bold direction; look around corners for ways to serve customers.

principles.name: Bias For Action
principles.description: Speed matters and is a leadership decision, not a circumstance. Most decisions are reversible two-way doors — make them quickly at the team level. Reserve deep study for one-way doors. Days or hours, not weeks.

principles.name: Frugality
principles.description: Accomplish more with less. Constraints breed resourcefulness, self-sufficiency, and invention. No extra points for headcount, budget, or fixed expense.

principles.name: Earn Trust
principles.description: Listen attentively, speak candidly, treat others respectfully. Be vocally self-critical, even when awkward; benchmark against the best.

principles.name: Deep Dive
principles.description: Operate at all levels and stay connected to the details; audit frequently; be skeptical when metrics and anecdotes differ. It is hard to fake the details in a narrative — that is why the narrative format works.

principles.name: Have Backbone
principles.description: Respectfully challenge decisions when you disagree, even when uncomfortable. No compromise for social cohesion. Once decided, commit wholly.

principles.name: Deliver Results
principles.description: Focus on the key inputs and deliver with the right quality, on time. Launch is the starting line, not the finish.

principles.name: Strive To Be Earths Best Employer
principles.description: Work to create a safer, more productive, more diverse, and more just work environment; lead with empathy and make others' success possible.

principles.name: Success And Scale Bring Broad Responsibility
principles.description: Big things carry big obligations: be humble about second-order effects, better every day for customers, employees, communities, and the world, and leave things better than found.

workflows.name: aws-two-way-door
workflows.description: Amazon Working Backwards with two-way-door ceremony — for reversible decisions (typically features, experiments, incremental bets). Starts with the human-authored Press Release (the same founding artifact regardless of scale), stress-tested by the FAQ; the iterative PR/FAQ review is the only formal gate and the 6-pager is optional. Optional post-FAQ deepening: OpportunitySpec (discovery, feature scale) or MRD (market validation, product scale) — the door sets the ceremony; the scale picks the tool.

methodology.name: Amazon Working Backwards (Feature)
methodology.description:
Amazon uses the same PR/FAQ instrument for features as for products; what
scales is ceremony (one-way vs. two-way door), not the sequence. At feature
scale the optional discovery deepening is the OpportunitySpec, which
combines Patton's discovery-focused Opportunity Canvas with Cagan's
business-case-focused SVPG Assessment.

press.description: The founding artifact: human-authored press release announcing the customer experience. Written first; everything else works backward from it.

bmc.guidance: Extract Business Model Canvas blocks from MRD sections 2-11. Format as standalone canvas for visual review.

faq.prompt_context:
Generate FAQ challenging the Press Release's claims. Include questions about:
- Users & Problem: Who is this for? Why is this a problem?
- Current Solutions: How do people solve this today?
- Competitive Edge: Why us? Why not competitors?
- Market & Timing: Why now?
- Critical Requirements: What must be true?
- Risks & Assumptions: What could go wrong?

mrd.guidance: Deepen and validate the FAQ's business-case answers with market evidence: segments, sizing, competition, positioning.

opportunity-spec.prompt_context:
Populate the 12-box OpportunitySpec canvas from the Press Release and FAQ:
- Users & Problem (Box 1) from the problem statement
- Solution Ideas (Box 3) from the announced experience
- User Value (Box 4) from the headline benefit
- Business Value (Box 5) and Competitive Edge (Box 6) from differentiation claims
- Success Metrics (Box 9) from measurable outcomes
Flag boxes the source documents leave unanswered — those are the discovery gaps.

prd.guidance: Derive product requirements from the announced customer experience (press) and its stress-tested constraints (FAQ), grounded in whichever optional deepening is present: the discovery canvas (OpportunitySpec, typical at feature scale) or market validation (MRD, typical at product scale).

trd.guidance: Technical design to support PRD requirements.

workflows.name: big-tech
workflows.description:
Comprehensive "best of all worlds" profile combining practices from 10 leading methodologies:
- AWS Working Backwards (customer obsession, PR/FAQ, 6-pager)
- Google Design Docs (OKRs, tradeoffs, alternatives, experimentation)
- Stripe API-First (developer experience, documentation quality)
- Netflix Freedom & Responsibility (context not control, transparency)
- Spotify Bets (autonomous squads, fail fast)
- Meta (move fast, bold bets)
- Apple (DRI, focus)
- Microsoft (growth mindset, accessibility)
- Basecamp Shape Up (appetite, pitches, hill charts, circuit breaker)
- Teresa Torres Continuous Discovery (weekly touchpoints, OST, assumption testing)

workflows.name: pbhq-lite
workflows.description: ProductBuildersHQ Lite: the smallest spec set that keeps product, technology, plan, and roadmap distinct — PRD (what), TRD (how), PLAN (sequencing), ROADMAP (tracking). The four stay separate because they answer different questions and change on different cadences; merging any two couples their churn. Built to keep velocity high and development consistent across one-person, multi-repo initiatives: minimal ceremony keeps the loop turning fast, and the same four files committed alongside the code in every repo let humans and agents navigate any initiative the same way. This is the minimal set for the building phase — getting to shipped with verifiable success criteria; growth-phase product execution (GTM plans, growth experiments) adds artifacts or graduates to a heavier workflow rather than stretching these four.

plan.description: Implementation plan - the narrative of the sequence: why this order, dependencies, phases, milestones. Deliberately separate from ROADMAP so the plan's story is not churned by status flips

prd.description: Product Requirements Document - defines the what: problem, goals, non-goals, user stories, functional requirements, and required success metrics (outcome targets with baselines and measurement method — the Product Loop's verification criteria)

roadmap.description: Execution tracking - the checklist: a machine-readable RMI ledger (stable IDs, status, progress) committed with the repo. Deliberately separate from PLAN so per-session status churn never touches the narrative

trd.description: Technical Requirements Document - defines the how: architecture, components, APIs, data models, security considerations

plan.guidance: Sequence implementation based on dependencies from TRD and priorities from PRD. Break into phases with clear deliverables.

roadmap.guidance: Create RMI entries for each plan item. Use stable IDs (RMI-REPOSLUG-NNN). Track status alongside code commits.

trd.guidance: Derive technical approach from PRD requirements. Include architecture decisions, component boundaries, and API contracts.

workflows.name: quick-fix
workflows.description: Minimal workflow for small fixes and maintenance tasks. Only the ROADMAP (the machine-readable RMI ledger) is required, so a fix can be tracked and shipped without spec ceremony. PRD, TRD, and PLAN remain available as optional documents when a fix turns out to need more context.

workflows.description: V2MOM strategic planning framework (Vision, Values, Methods, Obstacles, Measures). Supports cascading alignment from Company → Department → Team → Individual levels.

v2mom-alignment.description: Synthesized document showing alignment to parent V2MOM methods.

v2mom-measures.description: Quantifiable metrics. Each measure should map to KPIs in ProductContext.

v2mom-methods.description: Actions and initiatives. Each method should map to capabilities in ProductContext.

v2mom-obstacles.description: Known blockers and risks. Each obstacle should have mitigation strategies.

v2mom-summary.description: Unified V2MOM document combining all sections with cross-references.

v2mom-values.description: Ranked list of beliefs and priorities. Higher-ranked values take precedence in trade-offs.

v2mom-vision.description: The north star - what we want to achieve. Should be inspiring, clear, and memorable.

v2mom-alignment.guidance:
Show how this V2MOM's vision supports the parent's methods.
Include:
- Which parent methods this V2MOM advances
- Contribution to parent metrics
- Dependencies on sibling V2MOMs

v2mom-measures.guidance:
Define quantifiable metrics for each method.
For each measure:
- Be specific and measurable (SMART)
- Include baseline, target, and stretch goals
- Define measurement frequency
- Link to KPIs in ProductContext

v2mom-methods.guidance:
Define specific initiatives that advance the vision while honoring the values.
For each method:
- Link to ProductContext capabilities when applicable
- Include clear ownership
- Define success criteria
- Estimate effort/timeline

v2mom-obstacles.guidance:
Identify challenges that could block methods from succeeding.
For each obstacle:
- Categorize: technical, organizational, market, resource
- Define mitigation strategies
- Assign owner for resolution
- Link to related decisions in ProductContext

v2mom-summary.guidance:
Create a unified V2MOM document with:
- Executive summary
- All five sections with cross-references
- ProductContext entity links
- Parent V2MOM alignment (if applicable)

v2mom-values.guidance:
Extract the core beliefs and principles that will guide achieving the vision.
Values should be:
- Ranked in priority order (1 = highest)
- Actionable trade-off guides ("customer success over short-term revenue")
- Consistent with organizational values

integrations.name: AWS AI-DLC Workflows
integrations.description: AI-Driven Development Life Cycle — a prompt/rules package that steers an AI coding agent through Inception, Construction, and Operations phases, emitting reviewable markdown artifacts at each human-gated stage. Not a CLI or MCP server: activated in-agent with the phrase "Using AI-DLC, ...".

artifacts.description: Primary state tracker — project info, extension config, and the "## Stage Progress" checklist. Definitive marker that a run has occurred.
Append-only, timestamped log of every interaction.
Analyzed requirements — the hinge every downstream stage builds on.
Which downstream stages run, their depth, and a workflow visualization.
Components, methods, services, and dependency maps (conditional).
Per-unit business logic, domain entities, and rules.
Markdown summaries of generated code (the code itself lands at the workspace root).
Build and test instruction files plus a summary.
Application code, tests, and IaC written to the workspace root.

lifecycle.name: Inception
lifecycle.description: Planning — WHAT & WHY. Workspace detection, (brownfield) reverse engineering, requirements analysis, user stories, workflow planning, application design, and units-of-work generation.

lifecycle.name: Construction
lifecycle.description: HOW — per unit of work: functional design, NFR requirements and design, infrastructure design, code generation, then build and test.

lifecycle.name: Operations
lifecycle.description: Reserved for deployment and monitoring (placeholder in current release).

status.description: Parse the "## Stage Progress" checklist in aidlc-state.md (respecting SKIPPED as done/not-applicable), then refine per-unit progress from the checkbox ratio in each construction/plans/<unit>-code-generation-plan.md. Formats are LLM-generated markdown — match checkboxes plus the keywords COMPLETED/SKIPPED/IN PROGRESS rather than exact headings.

inputs.description: Vision Document (what to build and why) plus a Technical Environment Document, consumed at Requirements Analysis. An external PRD/6-pager maps onto the Vision Document.

outputs.description: Application code, tests, and IaC at the workspace root.
The aidlc-docs/ markdown tree (requirements, design, plans, state).

integrations.name: AWS Kiro Spec-Driven Development
integrations.description: Kiro is an agentic IDE whose spec workflow turns a prompt into a three-file spec — requirements (EARS notation), design, and tasks — then implements task by task. Modeled from published documentation and the IDE (no public source repository), so the on-disk detail is lower-confidence than repo-modeled tools.

artifacts.description: Steering documents — standing project conventions and guidance.
Feature requirements in EARS notation (user stories + acceptance criteria).
Technical design — architecture, components, data models, sequencing.
Discrete, checkboxed implementation tasks linked to requirements.
Source code implemented task by task from tasks.md.

lifecycle.name: Steering
lifecycle.description: Optional standing guidance the agent applies across specs.

lifecycle.name: Requirements
lifecycle.description: Capture requirements in EARS notation from a feature prompt.

lifecycle.name: Design
lifecycle.description: Produce the technical design from the approved requirements.

lifecycle.name: Tasks
lifecycle.description: Break the design into discrete implementation tasks.

lifecycle.name: Implement
lifecycle.description: Execute tasks one at a time, updating task status.

status.description: Percent complete = checked over total tasks in tasks.md. Phase is inferable from which of requirements.md / design.md / tasks.md exist for a feature.

inputs.description: Feature idea given in the IDE. An external definition-side PRD feeds the requirements phase (or is merged into requirements.md).

outputs.description: Source code implemented from the task list.

integrations.name: OpenSpec
integrations.description: Lightweight, brownfield-first SDD layer where humans and AI agents agree on written specs (requirements + scenarios) before code, using delta-based change proposals (ADDED/MODIFIED/REMOVED) that merge into a canonical spec set on archive. Current workflow surface is branded OPSX.

artifacts.description: Project config — schema, context, and per-artifact rules injected into generation.
Canonical, agreed-upon behavior — the source of truth (Requirements + WHEN/THEN scenarios).
The why + what of a change (intent, scope, capabilities, impact).
Technical how — context, decisions, risks, migration (optional).
Completed changes, date-prefixed, retained for history.

lifecycle.name: Init
lifecycle.description: Scaffold the openspec/ directory and config.

lifecycle.name: Explore
lifecycle.description: Optional shaping/thinking step before proposing (no structured output).

lifecycle.name: Propose
lifecycle.description: Open a change — proposal, delta specs, optional design, and tasks.

lifecycle.name: Apply
lifecycle.description: Implement the change, checking off tasks as code is written.

lifecycle.name: Archive
lifecycle.description: Merge delta specs into the canonical specs and move the change to archive/.

status.description: A change directly under openspec/changes/ is active; under openspec/changes/archive/ it is done (date-prefixed). For an active change, "openspec status --change <id> --json" reports each planning artifact as done/ready/blocked; implementation progress comes from tasks.md checkbox counts. Roll up: count active vs archived changes and specs/*/spec.md.

inputs.description: Human intent handed to /opsx:propose. An external PRD/feature request maps onto proposal.md (its Why / What Changes / Capabilities sections); standing product context maps onto openspec/config.yaml's context block.

outputs.description: The evolving canonical capability spec set (the durable product).
Implemented code, tracked via tasks.md checkboxes.

integrations.name: GitHub Spec-Kit
integrations.description: Spec-first toolkit ("Specify") that drives any AI coding agent from a natural-language feature description through specification, planning, and task breakdown to implementation. Spans its own requirements and design, but in the ProductBuildersHQ system the definition-side spec feeds its /speckit.specify step.

artifacts.description: Project governing principles, ratified and versioned.
Feature specification (WHAT/WHY) — user stories, FR-###, SC-### success criteria.
Implementation plan (HOW) — technical context and Constitution Check gate.
Entities, fields, relationships, and state transitions.
API/interface contracts (directory; may be absent for internal-only work).
Ordered, checkboxed task list grouped by phase and user story.
Source code and tests written during implementation.

lifecycle.name: Constitution
lifecycle.description: Establish project governing principles.

lifecycle.name: Specify
lifecycle.description: Turn a feature description into a structured specification.

lifecycle.name: Clarify
lifecycle.description: Resolve open questions in the spec (recommended before planning).

lifecycle.name: Plan
lifecycle.description: Produce the implementation plan and Phase 0/1 design docs.

lifecycle.name: Tasks
lifecycle.description: Break the plan into an ordered task list.

lifecycle.name: Analyze
lifecycle.description: Cross-artifact consistency check before implementation.

lifecycle.name: Implement
lifecycle.description: Execute tasks, writing code and marking tasks complete.

status.description: Percent complete = checked over total checkbox lines in tasks.md ("- [X]" or "- [x]" vs "- [ ]"). Phase is also inferable from which artifacts exist: spec only → specified; +plan → planned; +tasks → ready to implement.

inputs.description: Natural-language feature description passed to /speckit.specify. An external definition-side PRD feeds in here (or is merged into spec.md).

outputs.description: Source code and tests written into the repository.

pipelines.name: AWS Working Backwards → AI-DLC
pipelines.description: Definition side runs Amazon Working Backwards (aws-one-way-door) to produce the six-pager, PRD, and TRD; the execution side hands those to AWS AI-DLC, whose Requirements Analysis absorbs them as the Vision and drives Construction.

handoffs.transform: Distill the six-pager into the Vision Document consumed at Requirements Analysis.
Fold product requirements into the AI-DLC requirements analysis.
Seed per-unit functional and NFR design from the technical requirements.

pipelines.name: Big Tech Product → OpenSpec
pipelines.description: A Big Tech product definition produces a PRD and six-pager; OpenSpec's /opsx:propose consumes them into a change proposal, then delta specs, tasks, and implementation, archiving into the canonical capability specs.

handoffs.transform: Map PRD scope onto proposal.md Why / What Changes / Capabilities.
Use the six-pager narrative as the proposal's context and rationale.

pipelines.name: PBHQ Lite → Spec-Kit
pipelines.description: A lightweight PBHQ Lite definition produces a reconciled spec; Spec-Kit's /speckit.specify consumes it (or it is merged into specs/<feature>/spec.md), after which plan → tasks → implement proceeds.

handoffs.transform: Pass the reconciled spec as the /speckit.specify argument, or merge it into specs/<feature>/spec.md.

loop_systems.name: AWS AI-DLC Single-Loop System
loop_systems.description: The AI-DLC development cycle as published by AWS — a single human-gated AI loop. In ProductBuildersHQ terms it is an engineering (Builder) loop: the task arrives from outside the system, and "verify outcome" checks the work matches the task, not whether the task achieved its product goal. Included as the reference system the two-loop model generalizes.

loops.name: AI-DLC Cycle
loops.question: Matches the task?
loops.description: Humans provide and gate; AI plans and executes.

stations.name: Humans Provide Task
stations.description: A task arrives from outside the loop.

stations.name: AI Creates Plan
stations.description: AI drafts a plan and seeks clarification.

stations.name: AI Refines Plan
stations.description: The plan is revised with the clarifications.

stations.name: Humans Approve Plan
stations.description: Explicit human approval gate before execution.

stations.name: Humans Verify Outcome
stations.description: Humans verify the work matches the task, then the cycle repeats.

loop_systems.name: ProductBuildersHQ Two-Loop System
loop_systems.description: The Product Loop originates what to build and verifies outcomes; the Builder Loop implements and verifies built-right. Both loops share the same gate anatomy — intent, AI drafts, clarify, approve, AI executes, verify — and differ in artifact (specs vs code) and verification question (right thing? vs built right?). Gates shift from human to policy authority as a team's autonomy (ASDM level) rises. Generalizes single-loop systems such as AWS AI-DLC, which map onto the Builder Loop.

loops.name: Product Loop
loops.question: Right thing?
loops.description: Humans use AI to originate what to build and to verify the built work achieves its goal — adoption, engagement, revenue.

stations.name: Sense
stations.description: Market signals, user research, and production telemetry arriving from the Builder Loop.

stations.name: Hypothesize
stations.description: Frame opportunities and hypotheses worth testing.

stations.name: Define
stations.description: AI drafts the definition specs — MRD, Press Release, FAQ, 6-Pager, PRD, UXD — with a human clarification sub-cycle and LLM-as-a-Judge evaluation.

stations.name: Approve
stations.description: Humans approve the Product Baseline — the handoff contract to the Builder Loop.
stations.autonomy_note: Remains human at every autonomy level; the human's market knowledge advantage is largest here.

stations.name: Measure
stations.description: Instrument adoption, engagement, and revenue against the hypothesis.

stations.name: Validate & Grow
stations.description: Verify the hypothesis survived contact with users; double down or kill. Learnings feed Sense.

loops.name: Builder Loop
loops.question: Built right?
loops.description: AI implements against the handed-off specs under human-or-policy gates. Execution workflows (AI-DLC, Spec-Kit, OpenSpec, Kiro) instantiate this loop; the agentic coding loop runs inside Build.

stations.name: Accept
stations.description: Receive the Product Baseline; the builder accepts the spec as buildable.

stations.name: Plan
stations.description: AI drafts the implementation plan, running the clarify sub-cycle. Spec ambiguity escalates to the Product Loop rather than being resolved by builder guesswork.

stations.name: Approve
stations.autonomy_note: Human at L5 and below; policy-gated at L6+.

stations.name: Build
stations.description: AI executes — code, tests, iterate. The agentic coding loop runs unattended inside this station.

stations.name: Verify
stations.description: Built-right verification against spec and scenarios.
stations.autonomy_note: Human review at L5 and below; LLM-as-a-Judge and scenario validation at L6.

stations.name: Ship
stations.description: Release per operational policy; emits telemetry to the Product Loop.
stations.autonomy_note: Human gates through L6; autonomous operations at L7.

seams.description: The versioned handoff contract between product and builder (PDLC).
Usage, adoption, and operational data flowing back to the Product Loop.
Ambiguities in the spec escalate to the Product Loop instead of being resolved by builder guesswork.
